premises.text: Clean-energy transition and battery growth create exploding demand for lithium that current brine extraction cannot efficiently meet
premises.evidence_span: lithium brine industry lack efficient lithium extraction technology to meet the current demands of exploding battery market

premises.text: Solar evaporation of brine uses huge water volumes, emits carbon, takes years, and costs about $6,000 per metric ton
premises.evidence_span: to just produce one metric ton of lithium, they use up 500,000 gallons of water, releasing 5,000 kilograms of carbon, with a production cost of $6,000

premises.text: Nano-mosaic absorbents selectively attract lithium and reject other minerals, enabling a two-step process to battery-grade lithium within 48 hours
premises.evidence_span: These sponge-like materials are chemically and physically designed to just attract lithium, rejecting all other minerals

premises.text: The process uses far less water, about $1,000 per ton production cost, and zero carbon emission versus evaporation
premises.evidence_span: only 30,000 gallons of water is used, with a production cost of $1,000, with zero carbon emission

premises.text: Filter units with the absorbents can treat large brine volumes and extract multiple metric tons of lithium per day
premises.evidence_span: our filter units, which can treat almost 171 gallons of water per minute, extracting two metric tons of lithium per day
